### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b79e9e914998edb459ee52b50eac3231377609f0` — the merge of head `c8f1e79c94754e67169f969de12170f8125a23ed` into base `6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b79e9e914998edb459ee52b50eac3231377609f0 && git checkout b79e9e914998edb459ee52b50eac3231377609f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3 c8f1e79c94754e67169f969de12170f8125a23ed && git checkout -B drift-repro 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3 && git merge --no-ff c8f1e79c94754e67169f969de12170f8125a23ed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2faaebe929ab4463d78424b57819e3ded3ad9eb7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-namespace-name.test.ts + packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `claimedArtifactSlots`, `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE`, the artifact boot door), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`AssembledPackageBodySchema`, `assembledPackageBodyShape`, `composeStacks` preserve), packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, the eleven element schemas (app, page, dashboard, report, book, sharing, queue, assignment-rule, tool, hook, analytics cube), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts `uninstallPackage` / `unregisterItemsByPackage` / `forgetBareNameClaims` / `restoringOnRefusal` (live, outside the hunks), packages/objectql/src/registry-namespace-co-owner-names.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md (D2, child N row), scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__namespace-co-owner-names.ts.json, examples/app-multi-package/objectstack.config.ts. The changeset `.changeset/31720-residual-namespace-names.md` is a prose face: read for ②, not reviewed. Code outside the diff was read to judge the narrowing, never reviewed.

Inputs: card #31720 (body and all four comments: triage 6728959174, unblock 6729750199, claim 6729778749, os-dev-report 6731329179), PR #31767 (body, six-file list, net diff against `main` at `c2bb879f`), the check-runs on the head. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not read.

Check-runs on `2faaebe9` at the time of this record (03:21Z): `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Live E2E UI` success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success, `Test UI` success, `Check Changeset` success, `Check PR Size` success, `PR-body guards` success; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` skipped (no `ui/` path in the diff). `Test Core` is still PENDING: shard 6/8 success, shards 1–5, 7 and 8 `in_progress`. The gate set is not yet whole-green; this record does not stand in for the pending shards.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the live tree:

1. The `manifest` service refuses a `packages[]` stack whose residual (the top-level items `unclaimedTopLevel` leaves to the stack's own id) declares a covered `(type, name)` that an installed package of `stack.manifest.namespace` holds; `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, 422, every holder named; the whole artifact put back by the one `restoringOnRefusal` run — **right**. The refuse call sits after every `registerApp` and before `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` / `registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems`, so it reads the stack's own bodies' records too and nothing of the residual has registered when it throws. The predicate is N's (`namespaceNameConflicts`, `namespaceNameConflictMessage`); `residualNamespacePackageOf` rebuilds a body-shaped record keyed by `singularToPlural(type)` and hands it to `declaredNamespaceUniqueNames`, so the names are read the way N reads a package's — no second predicate.
2. The package door refuses a package whose covered name a registered stack's residual of the same namespace already holds, naming the stack's owner id — **right**. `refuseNamespaceHolderConflicts` appends `residualNamespaceHolders` of the incoming namespace to `sitting`; `namespaceNameConflicts` dedups holder ids, so a residual whose owner id is also a body id (the `preserve` shape, see ④) is named once.
3. The same stack registering again is not judged against its own residual (`other.packageId === incoming.packageId` skip) and replaces its own entry (`Map.set` by owner id) — **right**.
4. A refused stack records no holder: `recordResidualNamespaceHolder` is called after the run returns, so a throw never reaches it — **right** (pinned by the "refused stack records no holder" CONTROL).
5. A residual whose stack has no namespace or a shareable one (`base`, `system`, `sys`) is neither judged nor recorded (`isNamespaceJudged` at both calls) — **right**, N's rule unchanged and ADR-0150 D2's own exclusions (sys is the reserved kernel package; the environment package has no namespace).
6. A residual item of a type outside the twelve is not judged (`isNamespaceUniqueType` filter) — **right**. A top-level `job` is never residual because `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` carries no `jobs` key — **read and confirmed** (pinned).
7. Order independence between a stack and a package arriving later — **right** by 1 and 2 together.
8. **Wrong**: a recorded residual holder outlives its items on one real path. See ④ F1.
9. Public surface: `@objectstack/objectql` gains the export `residualNamespacePackageOf` and the type `ResidualItems`, and `SchemaRegistry` gains two public methods, `refuseResidualNamespaceNameConflicts` and `recordResidualNamespaceHolder` — additive, correctly carried by a `minor`. `ResidualItems` is structurally identical to the two fields of `@objectstack/metadata`'s `UnclaimedTopLevel` it reads (`ownerId: string | undefined`, `items: {type, item}[]`), so the engine's existing `residualAnswer` passes without an import from above the registry — **right**.
10. `os validate` / `os build` are unchanged. Judged under ③ (1): **right** on this head, with the jsdoc that says otherwise graded under ④ F2.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31720-residual-namespace-names.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; a `BREAKING` banner with Why / Before / Now / Who moves / Unchanged, the one-line fix (rename one of the two items, or declare it in one of the stack's packages), the first-party census (0 stacks with a residual of the covered types; `examples/app-multi-package` has no residual), and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. The diff publishes a narrowing of the accept set at the `manifest` service and at the package door, moves only `@objectstack/objectql` (cli untouched, so no cli bump is owed), and removes no key, export or field — so `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on the moved package, the breaking banner is owed and present, and no tombstone is owed. `Check Changeset` is green. **Matches.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm: nothing on base that is now refused was ever accepted for a reason other than the residual escaping N's door, and nothing is widened.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report's three `open_questions` and its one `out_of_scope_findings` entry, each answered:

1. **CLI half left unchanged (deviation from the card's "cli validate.ts / compile.ts" surface).** Verified in the live tree, not from the PR's account: `claimedArtifactSlots` claims a body's slot by `item.name`; N's `itemName` reads `name` first and falls to `id` only when `name` is absent; the eleven covered element schemas all declare `name` required (`SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` or a snake_case regex — app, page, dashboard, report, book, sharing rule, queue, assignment rule, tool, hook, cube), and every `packages[]` entry is gated whole by `ArtifactPackageSchema.safeParse` → `AssembledPackageBodySchema` = `ManifestSchema.extend(assembledPackageBodyShape())`, where `ManifestSchema` is closed and has no `navigation` key and `plugins` is an envelope key excluded from the body shape. So inside one artifact a body cannot hold a covered name without claiming its slot, and an item a body holds is by definition not residual (pinned for all eleven types). The only residual clash is with a package another artifact installed, which `findNamespaceNameRefusals` cannot see. **Option A accepted**: a CLI call could only ever answer `[]`, and the card's "it counts only when the stack's namespace equals one of its packages' namespaces, or another installed package's" is served by the engine door alone. Two consequences for the record: the jsdoc on this head must not claim the CLI judges the residual (④ F2), and the CLI module's own bound sentence on `main` ("the residual … is not judged at either door") is now half-stale and should be corrected when that file is next touched (follow-up; outside this diff).
2. **A stack with no namespace or a shareable one is not judged.** **Option A accepted**: identical to N's holder rule and to ADR-0150 D2 (sys is the kernel package, the environment package has no address); judging it would be a narrowing beyond D2, the maintainer's to rule.
3. **Names** (`residualNamespacePackageOf`, `ResidualItems`, `SchemaRegistry.refuseResidualNamespaceNameConflicts`, `recordResidualNamespaceHolder`; no new error code). **Option A accepted.** Reusing `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` is correct: the condition and the remedy are N's.
4. **Out of scope per dev: the anchor invariant** (`scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__namespace-co-owner-names.ts.json`) names `installPackage` and `os validate / os build` as the predicate's callers and not the manifest service's residual call. Read: `check:adr-anchors` is green on the head and the invariant's "never" list is not contradicted by the diff. Accepted as a one-sentence follow-up riding on the F1/F2 delta or a follow-up card; not a finding of its own.

No other dev flag or deviation is open. "HotCRM census NOT MEASURED" is stated in the PR body and the changeset; the first-party count is 0 and the maintainer's HotCRM measurement for D2 (0 of 297) is the ADR's. "Base side of Clause-② measured by ablation" is an acceptable measurement for a pure refusal insertion whose removal is the base.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main` (ADR-0150 D2, ruled 6724570466; #31717's namespace-co-owner-names rule): D2 says that within a namespace a behavioural `(type, name)` has at most one package holder so that `NAMESPACE/NAME` names one item. On `main`, a `packages[]` stack's residual registers under the stack's own id through `registerItem(type, item, 'name', ownerId)` with no package record and no pass through `installPackage`, so a residual `crm/home` beside a co-owner's `crm/home` was two items at one address — the spec's own refusal, not made real for this holder kind. This PR makes it real at the one door every stack registration reaches (the `manifest` service; `@objectstack/metadata` cannot import `@objectstack/objectql`, so the judge cannot sit in `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`) and makes the residual a holder for what arrives after it. It takes no declared capability away at the consumer: nothing in `skills/**`, the ADR or the stack schema declares that a stack's top level may repeat a name a co-owner holds, and the refusal text carries the rule and the remedy. The three epic red lines: resolution never loosens (only refusals are added); ambiguity is reported, never guessed (every holder named, `conflicts[]` structured); independently releasable (readings a–d stated and consistent with the tree). The twelve types only; no package-scoped resolution. Attempts to break it:

- A body item carrying `id` but no `name` (N's fallback) sneaking past the slot claim: refused by the closed body parse — see ③ (1). Holds.
- A manifest-as-app row on a body (`name` + `navigation`): `navigation` is not a `ManifestSchema` key. Holds.
- A stack whose owner id equals one body's id (the `preserve` shape: `composeStacks` sets `composed.manifest = selectManifest(stacks, 'last')`, so `examples/app-multi-package`'s owner is `com.example.multi.core`, a body): the predicate's same-id skip makes body and residual one holder, which is the changeset's own "Unchanged" line and D2-correct. Holds at install. Fails at uninstall — F1.
- A refusal inside the run restoring the registry while `residualNamespaceHolders` is outside the restore point: the record call is after the run, so no entry is written on a refusal; the refuse call only reads. Holds.
- The metadata door registering the residual into the metadata service before the engine door refuses (artifact boot: `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, then the runtime's `manifest.register`): pre-existing shape shared with N's package door; on a boot the refusal fails the boot, so no divergent state survives. Read, not a finding of this PR.

Findings:

- **F1 — should-fix — `registry.ts`: a recorded residual holder survives the withdrawal of the items it stands for.** `uninstallPackage(id)` calls `unregisterItemsByPackage(id)`, which deletes every registry key prefixed `${id}:` — and the residual's items are registered under exactly `ownerId` as their package id (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems` → `registerItem(type, …, 'name', ownerId)`; `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` likewise). When the owner id names one of the bodies — the normal `preserve` shape, measured on `examples/app-multi-package` — uninstalling that body withdraws the residual's items too, but `residualNamespaceHolders` keeps the entry: the next package of the namespace declaring that name is refused at the package door naming a holder that holds nothing. N pins the opposite for packages ("an uninstall takes its names with it", `registry-namespace-co-owner-names.test.ts`), and `uninstallPackage` already forgets every other per-id claim (`forgetBareNameClaims`, `forgetSecurityCatalogClaims`, `forgetDefaultRecordPageClaims`). The PR's stated bound ("its holder stays while its items stay registered") does not hold on this path. Not a must-fix: resolution is not loosened (an over-refusal, red line 1 intact), no stored shape is affected, and a restart rebuilds the map. Fix: drop `residualNamespaceHolders.delete(id)` into `uninstallPackage` beside `forgetBareNameClaims(id)` (downstream of the one refusing step), with a pin "uninstalling the residual's owner frees the residual's names". A delta review of that fix is owed on the new head.
- **F2 — should-fix — `namespace-co-owner-names.ts` header, the new "## The residual (#31720)" paragraph** states that the same predicate judges the residual "in `os validate` / `os build` against the stack's bodies". On this head it does not (③ 1), and the CLI module's own header says the residual is judged at neither door. A module docblock the ADR anchor governs advertising a check the runtime does not run is the Prime Directive 10 shape (declared, not delivered). Fix: name the one door that judges it (the `manifest` service) and state the CLI bound (inside one artifact the residual cannot share a covered name with a body; other artifacts' packages are invisible there). Rides on F1's delta; while there, the anchor invariant may gain its one sentence (③ 4).
- **Nit — test title** `'CONTROL — a residual item of a type outside the twelve is not judged (a dataset alpha also holds)'`: the assertion is `not.toBe('NAMESPACE_CONFLICT')`, which also passes if the dataset is refused for some other reason; a `toBeUndefined()` on `err?.message` would pin acceptance. No effect on the contract; accepted deviation.

No must-fix. Two should-fix findings: the round does not end here; the fix moves the head and this record no longer covers it — a delta review on the new head closes it.
